local.body: Hatchlight looks at your computer and picks the version of each model that runs best on it. Download it once, and every picture after that costs nothing and never leaves your machine. Models run on Windows and on Macs with Apple Silicon. On Linux they run on NVIDIA (CUDA) and the CPU, and that support is early and still being tested.

server.access.body: Use it on your home network, or from anywhere with Tailscale, which we recommend: HTTPS, and nothing opened to the internet. A domain behind Caddy or a Cloudflare Tunnel works too.
server.access.title: Reach it from anywhere
server.accounts.body: Each person signs in and sees only their own pictures. You decide who may train LoRAs and who may spend on paid models, up to a monthly limit.
server.accounts.title: Accounts, kept apart
server.agents.html: AI agents such as Claude Code connect over MCP, with an API token you make in Settings and limit to what they may do. The guide has the details.
server.needs.body: Linux or Windows with Docker, an NVIDIA card with driver 570 or newer, and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Without a card, models run on the processor, more slowly.
server.needs.title: You need:
server.note: Put Hatchlight on a home server or NAS with an NVIDIA card, and everyone at home or on your team uses it in the browser, each with their own account. One graphics card and one set of models, shared fairly.
server.quickNote: The second line builds the image. From the next release, a ready image comes from GitHub and that line can be skipped. Then open the address and enter the setup code from docker compose logs.
server.safety.body: Saved API keys are encrypted, the server's data is readable by the server alone, and the app runs in its container without root or special permissions.
server.safety.title: Careful by default
server.title: Run it on your own server.
services.note: Connect the services you use and pay them directly, at their prices. Hatchlight adds nothing on top.
services.title: Bring your own keys. No middleman.

vs.comfyui.cloud: Optional Partner Nodes call closed models such as OpenAI, Kling and Luma, with a Comfy account and credits. Comfy Cloud runs ComfyUI on cloud GPUs.
vs.comfyui.description: ComfyUI or Hatchlight? Node graphs and custom nodes, or one prompt compared across models side by side. Where each one is better, from official sources.
vs.comfyui.development: Very actively developed, with frequent releases.
vs.comfyui.extend: Custom nodes from a large community, installed and updated with ComfyUI-Manager. Workflows are saved as JSON, and a file made with ComfyUI brings its workflow back when dropped on the canvas.
vs.comfyui.heading: Hatchlight or ComfyUI?
vs.comfyui.install: Comfy Desktop (recommended), a portable build for Windows, or a manual install with Python.
vs.comfyui.intro: ComfyUI is a powerful, modular tool for image, video, audio and 3D models: you build workflows as a graph of nodes and extend it with custom nodes. Hatchlight is simpler: you type a prompt, choose models and compare what they make side by side. Both are free, open source, and run models on your own computer.
vs.comfyui.local: Windows, Linux and macOS, on NVIDIA, AMD (ROCm), Intel Arc and Apple Silicon, among others. Runs fully offline: the core downloads nothing unless you ask.
vs.comfyui.models: Images, video, audio and 3D: Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Wan 2.1 and 2.2, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, Hunyuan3D and more. It supports the latest open models natively.
vs.comfyui.name: ComfyUI
vs.comfyui.pickThem.one: You want full control: build your own pipelines node by node, and change every step.
vs.comfyui.pickThem.three: You want the workflows and custom nodes that its large community shares.
vs.comfyui.pickThem.title: When to pick ComfyUI
vs.comfyui.pickThem.two: You want the newest open models, or audio and 3D: ComfyUI supports many more models than Hatchlight.
vs.comfyui.pickUs.one: You want to type a prompt and see what several models make, side by side, with each one's time and cost.
vs.comfyui.pickUs.three: You want cloud models on your own keys without an account, an assistant you can talk to, or an MCP server for AI agents.
vs.comfyui.pickUs.two: You would rather not build a graph or manage Python: Hatchlight picks the version of each model that fits your graphics card.

vs.comfyui.title: Hatchlight vs ComfyUI: an honest comparison
vs.comfyui.what: A node-graph interface, API and backend for diffusion models. You build each workflow from nodes and can save and reuse it.
vs.fooocus.cloud: None: models run on your computer, or on Google Colab.
vs.fooocus.description: Looking for a Fooocus alternative? Fooocus now gets bug fixes only and stays on SDXL. How Hatchlight compares, and when Fooocus is still the right pick.
vs.fooocus.development: Limited long-term support: bug fixes only. The last release, 2.5.5, came out in 2024.
vs.fooocus.extend: Styles, inpaint and outpaint with its own inpaint model, image prompts, upscale and variations.
vs.fooocus.heading: Hatchlight or Fooocus?
vs.fooocus.install: On Windows, a download to extract and run; on Linux and Mac, an install with Python. Google Colab and Docker too.
vs.fooocus.intro: Fooocus is a simple image generator built on Stable Diffusion XL, made so that a prompt alone gives a good picture. Its README now says it is in limited long-term support, with bug fixes only, and will not add newer model architectures; for models such as FLUX it points to WebUI Forge, ComfyUI or SwarmUI. Hatchlight is also simple to use, and runs newer picture and video models.
vs.fooocus.local: Windows and Linux, on NVIDIA cards from 4 GB, and AMD in beta. Macs with Apple Silicon through an unofficial guide.
vs.fooocus.models: Stable Diffusion XL only. Its README says there are no plans to support newer model architectures.
vs.fooocus.name: Fooocus
vs.fooocus.pickThem.one: You use SDXL and like the pictures Fooocus makes with little tuning.
vs.fooocus.pickThem.three: It already works for you and you need nothing newer: bug fixes still come.
vs.fooocus.pickThem.title: When to pick Fooocus
vs.fooocus.pickThem.two: You want its styles, its inpaint model and its image prompts, all tuned for SDXL.
vs.fooocus.pickUs.one: You want models newer than SDXL: FLUX, Z-Image, Qwen-Image, and video with Wan.
vs.fooocus.pickUs.three: You want an app that is still growing, with cloud models on your own keys, a command line and an MCP server for AI agents.
vs.fooocus.pickUs.two: You want to send one prompt to several models and compare what they make, side by side.
vs.fooocus.title: Hatchlight vs Fooocus: an honest comparison
vs.fooocus.what: A simple image generator that needs little tuning: type a prompt, get a picture.
vs.sourcesNote.html: What this page says about the other app comes from its own pages, listed below. If something here is wrong or out of date, please open an issue.
vs.table.title: Side by side
vs.us.cloud: Optional, on your own keys: fal, Replicate, OpenRouter, OpenAI and Google Gemini, paid to them directly. No account.
vs.us.development: Actively developed, and young: fewer models, and Linux support is still early.
vs.us.extend: Edit by instruction, redraw a masked part, outpaint and upscale ×4. LoRAs, your own SDXL and SD 1.5 checkpoints, and LoRA training built in. No plugins.
vs.us.install: One installer, no Python; the installers are not signed yet. Also a command line, the npm package (bunx hatchlight) and a Docker image for a home server.
vs.us.license: MIT. No account and no telemetry.
vs.us.local: Windows (NVIDIA, AMD, other cards through Vulkan, CPU), Macs with Apple Silicon, and Linux (NVIDIA and CPU, still early). Intel Macs use cloud models only. Works offline once a model is downloaded.
vs.us.models: A catalog of picture and video models, among them SDXL, FLUX.1 schnell, FLUX.2 klein, Z-Image, Qwen-Image and Wan 2.2, each in versions sized for your memory. A new model arrives only once it is added to the catalog.
vs.us.what: A desktop app for pictures and videos: one prompt goes to several models, and the results appear side by side with their time and cost. No graph to build.
